title: Customer Forget API + Retention Rules Engine with Verifiable Deletion Receipts
creator: Sophia Alvarez
description: Build a customer-facing Forget API that ties into a new retention rules engine and emits cryptographically verifiable deletion receipts. The goal is to let tenants request targeted or bulk deletions (by user, by tenant, by object tag), validate policy eligibility, run a staged purge (dry-run -> schedule -> execute), and produce a WORM export of deletion checkpoints that customers and auditors can use to confirm completion. The system should support synchronous small deletes for low-latency UX and asynchronous bulk expunges for scale. It must respect residency boundaries (region-scoped deletes), legal holds, and retention overrides.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/forget -> returns request_id and immediate policy eligibility result
Policy engine: retention rules evaluate including inheritance, overrides, and geofence constraints
Modes: dry-run (preview counts), scheduled (cron/UTC), and immediate execution (subject to SLA and quota)
Receipts: each completed deletion produces a verifiable receipt (SHA256 chain + timestamp + region stamp) exportable as JSON and downloadable from Console
Observability: console shows request timeline, per-shard progress, failure reasons, and estimated completion time
Edge cases: legal-hold prevents execution and surfaces contact path; soft-delete window configurable per-tenant; rollback only permitted within configured window
E2E tests: simulated tenant with 10M rows completes in test infra and receipts validate against stored checksums
Security: API requires tenant-scoped auth and write audit log entries to the KMS-backed audit stream

notes: Trade-offs considered: synchronous immediate deletes improve UX but increase write amplification and risk slow tail latencies; decided to allow small synchronous deletes (<10k keys) and funnel large jobs to async pipeline.

Receipts format: JSON with fields {request_id, affected_count, region, timestamp, receipt_hash, verification_proof}. We'll provide a client tool to validate receipts against the public verification endpoint.
Quota: tenant forget requests will be rate-limited; bulk expunges require a support ticket for Dedicated/Private in MVP
Rollout plan: feature-flagged per-tenant -> pilot with two customers -> enable for self-serve tenants after 6 weeks of monitoring
risks: Risk: accidental cross-region deletes if residency tag mismatch. Mitigation: strict policy validation and require explicit region param for cross-zone ops.
Risk: receipts ledger growth. Mitigation: retention policy for receipts (retain compressed ledger for 3 years, exportable on demand).
Risk: legal conflict between customer request and compliance hold. Mitigation: legal-hold check as precondition that blocks execution and surfaces support path.
